dedupe_keys.name: world bank real time food prices rtfp monthly food price estimates by product and market

description: Real Time Food Prices is a World Bank series of monthly food price estimates by product and market for fragile and conflict-affected and other low-income countries, published as one Microdata Library entry per country. It combines prices measured by the World Food Programme, the Food and Agriculture Organization and national statistical offices with machine-learning estimates for missing months, and gives for each market and product a price, open, high, low and close values, a food price index, and the share of observed versus imputed data. The producer is the World Bank Development Economics Data Group (lead author Bo Pieter Johannes Andrée), in the Fragility, Conflict and Violence collection. Coverage varies by country; the Gambia entry read today covers 28 markets from 2007 to August 2026. Data download as CSV with DDI and JSON metadata and through the catalogue API, published as open data, free without restriction beyond citation. Caveats: a large share of values can be imputed (coverage and imputation rates are given per product), estimates are revised as new prices arrive, and the method smooths short shocks. Simulation uses: continuous price series to detect and model food market disruption after climate shocks and conflict, and inputs to early warning and food supply resilience models. Related records: the WFP Global Food Prices database (data-wfp-global-food-prices) supplies most observed prices.
